It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

As this Tribunal has already held that R1 was responsible for the death of the deceased due to his neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

Therefore, the petitioners have become entitled to be compensated for death of deceased in the above accident, but computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
COMPENSATION 18.

Basically only three facts need to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death : (a) age of the deceased; (b) income of the deceased; and the (c) the number of dependents.

The issues to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at the loss of dependency are (i)
additions/deductions to be made for arriving at the income; (ii) the deduction to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased; and (iii) the multiplier to be applied with reference of the age of the deceased.
If these determinants are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.

In this regard, though not quoted, reliance is placed upon, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.
(2009) 6 SCC 121.

sentences.text: As per claim petition, deceased was about 44 years old on the date of accident.
Deceased was a labour.
No document of educational qualification of deceased proved on record.
Therefore, the income of the deceased, as on the date of the accident, has been treated as that of an "Unskilled".
As per aadahr card, the address of the deceased is of Bihar.
However, a rent agreement has also been filed on record to show that the deceased was residing in the Delhi.
The rent agreement is of May,2015 whereas the accident occurred on 12.10.2021.
No document is proved on record to show that deceased was residing in Delhi at the time of accident.
Therefore, on the date of accident i.e 12.10.2021, the income of deceased has been treated as that of an unskilled in Bihar and the minimum wages of an unskilled in Bihar was Rs. 7,956/- per month.
Counsel for the petitioners further argued that future prospects should also be awarded to the petitioners as per law.
21. Accordingly, on the basis of aforementioned documents, age of the deceased is taken as 44 years as on the date of accident.

Hence, the multiplier of "14" would be applicable in view of pronouncement made in case titled as Sarla Verma (supra).
22.

opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so,
 to what amount and from whom?
My issue wise findings in the case are as under:-
ISSUE NO.1 1. Whether deceased Sikandar Sah expired due to injuries suffered in road traffic accident on 12.10.2021 at about 05:15 pm, at NH28, Dak Bangla Chowk, Near Pidoli due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing no. BR 09PA 3026 which was being driven by driver Sh. Navin Kumar Ray S/o Sh.
Pavitr Ray on the said date, time and place?
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?
Now, the question which arises for determination is as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
13.
Therefore, the case does not warrant any other best evidence.
Further, R1, after registration of FIR,
has not filed any complaint of his false implication in the FIR.
Keeping in view the facts & evidence produced by the petitioner, it is established that the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle being driven by respondent No.1, as a result of which, the deceased lost his life.
15. Futher, the fact that FIR was lodged against the respondent no.1 and he faced criminal charges of causing death and injuries by rash and negligent driving in the said accident is an adverse inference Sweeti Devi vs Navin Kumar Ray on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174713583/
5 on the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
The submission that R1 has been acquitted in an appeal has no bearing on the claim of the petitioner as in criminal case the burden on prosecution to prove the case is absolute doubt and the issue before Criminal Court is of criminal rashness and negligence, which is not before the Tribunal.
16.
As this Tribunal has already held that R1 was responsible for the death of the deceased due to his neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Therefore, the petitioners have become entitled to be compensated for death of deceased in the above accident, but computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
Basically only three facts need to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death : (a) age of the deceased; (b) income of the deceased; and the (c) the number of dependents.
The issues to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at the loss of dependency are (i)
additions/deductions to be made for arriving at the income; (ii) the deduction to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased; and (iii) the multiplier to be applied with reference of the age of the deceased.
If these determinants are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
In this regard, though not quoted, reliance is placed upon, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.
(2009) 6 SCC 121.
19.
Deceased was a labour.
No document of educational qualification of deceased proved on record.
Therefore, the income of the deceased, as on the date of the accident, has been treated as that of an "Unskilled".
Hence, the multiplier of "14" would be applicable in view of pronouncement made in case titled as Sarla Verma (supra).
22.
Considering the fact that deceased was aged about 44 years at the time of accident and was a labour, future prospects @ 25 % has to be awarded in favour of petitioners in view of recent pronouncement made by Constitutional Bench of Apex Court in the case titled as National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi & Ors., (2017) 16 MACT Case No. 91/2023 (FIR no.
306/2021) Sweeti Devi Vs. Navin Kumar Ray & Anr.

23.
Claimant/petitioners are wife and three children of deceased.
Therefore, as there are four dependents upon deceased there has to be deduction of "one forth (1/4th)", as per the mandate of Sarla Verma (supra).
After the judgment passed in National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi & Ors. (supra)
and recent judgment titled as New India MACT Case No. 91/2023 (FIR no. 306/2021) Sweeti Devi Vs. Navin Kumar Ray & Anr.
